cards.title: Radial oscillator eigenvalue and factor-two diagnostic
cards.role: Checks whether the spectrum used upstream of the plotted vacuum-energy formulas follows from the stated Klein-Gordon operator.

source_refs.value: Eqs. (4)-(11), TeX labels KGCompleta, KDE, integer_energy

checks.reason: The radial operator follows directly from paper Eqs. (4)-(6).
For l=n=0, direct substitution of R=exp(-alpha*rho^2/2) gives lambda=2 alpha, not alpha.
Both lambda and alpha have mass dimension two.

cards.numerical_form: radial_ground_eigenvalue(alpha) = 2*alpha; the paper value alpha is retained only as a documented source discrepancy.
open_questions: Paper Eq. (11) is inconsistent with the operator in Eqs. (4)-(6) by a factor of two.

cards.title: Dimensionless Landau-like boundary energy
cards.role: Defines the independently evaluated numerical object in paper Fig. 2(a), conditional on the paper's stated subtraction prescription.

checks.reason: Transcribed from paper Eq. (25), including its dimensionless normalization.
alpha0/sinh(alpha0*tau^2) tends to tau^-2 and recovers the standard massive Dirichlet result.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate on u=log(tau), sum j with the Jacobi/Poisson identity, and integrate the smooth vector integrand with adaptive Gauss-Kronrod quadrature.

cards.title: Dimensionless additional boundary energy
cards.role: Defines the independently evaluated numerical object in paper Fig. 2(b), conditional on the paper's stated subtraction prescription.

checks.reason: Transcribed from paper Eq. (27); alpha0 is used after tau is rescaled by L.
Only alpha0*tau^2 is dimensionless after the rescaling; the printed alpha*tau^2 in the first line is a notation typo.

cards.numerical_form: Use a stable reciprocal 4*alpha0*exp(-2*x)/[(1-exp(-2*x))*(1-exp(-x))], x=alpha0*tau^2, inside the log-tau quadrature.
open_questions: Paper Eqs. (18)-(19) print n starting at 1 in the second sum, whereas Eq. (26)'s closed-form denominator corresponds to n starting at 0.

cards.title: Independent positive Bessel-series representation
cards.role: Provides a numerically independent cross-check of both proper-time quadratures.

source_refs.value: Independent expansion of paper Eqs. (25) and (27)

checks.reason: Starts from the two displayed paper integrals.
Uses 1/sinh(x)=2 sum exp(-(2n+1)x), the product-series multiplicity floor(r/2), and the standard K1 integral.

cards.numerical_form: Directly sum positive K1 terms at selected alpha0,m0 points and compare against the Poisson-resummed quadrature.

cards.title: Correct small-coupling limits
cards.role: Checks the standard Casimir limit of the Landau sector and the singular power of the additional sector.

source_refs.value: Eqs. (32)-(36), TeX labels alphaS through alphaS_C

checks.reason: The paper gives the correct K2 expression for the Landau term but prints K2 rather than K3 for the additional term.
The additional denominator is order (alpha0*tau^2)^2, leaving a tau^-7 integral and therefore K3.
For m0=0, E_L dimensionless tends to -pi^4/180 and E_c tends to -2*zeta(6)/alpha0.

open_questions: Paper Eq. (36) has the wrong Bessel order and power of m0/j.

cards.title: Correct strong-coupling asymptotic
cards.role: Verifies exponential suppression and the correct square-root exponent for both energy sectors.

checks.reason: Paper Eq. (31) correctly reaches a K1 expression before printing an inconsistent final asymptotic.
Applying K1(z)~sqrt(pi/(2z))*exp(-z) gives a square-root alpha0 exponent and alpha0^(5/4) leading power.

open_questions: Paper Eq. (31)'s final line incorrectly changes exp(-2*j*sqrt(f*alpha0)) into exp(-2*j*f*alpha0).

cards.title: Total-to-Landau energy ratio
cards.role: Defines paper Fig. 3 and makes the additional sector's relative contribution explicit.

checks.reason: The ratio follows from E0=EL+Ec and is the observable named in the Fig. 3 caption.
The f=2 sector is more strongly suppressed, so the ratio tends to one at large alpha0.

cards.numerical_form: ratio = 1 + correction_energy / landau_energy, evaluated from two independently generated arrays.
